input.plan:
# Domain email for kuchup.com (Cloudflare Email Routing)

## Goal

Receive and send as `@kuchup.com` at $0 using the existing Cloudflare DNS zone. No mailbox product, no app code changes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  sender[External sender] -->|to hello@kuchup.com| cfMX[Cloudflare MX]
  cfMX --> route[Email Routing]
  route --> gmail[Your personal Gmail]
  gmail -->|Send as hello@ via smtp.gmail.com| world[Recipients]
```

## Current state

- DNS: Cloudflare (`blair` / `lochlan` NS)
- Web: proxied A records for apex / www / mcp
- Mail: **no MX**, no SPF/DKIM/DMARC (only Google Search Console TXT)
- Existing GSC TXT must stay untouched when editing DNS

## Addresses (default)

| Address | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `hello@kuchup.com` | Public / product contact |
| `support@kuchup.com` | User help |
| Catch-all → same Gmail | Don’t miss typos / random `@kuchup.com` |

Destination: one personal Gmail (verify ownership in Cloudflare). Add more destinations later if needed.

## Step 1 — Enable Cloudflare Email Routing

In Cloudflare → **kuchup.com** → **Email** → **Email Routing**:

1. Enable / onboard domain (Cloudflare auto-adds MX + routing SPF/DKIM).
2. Confirm mail records are **DNS only** (grey cloud) — never orange-proxy MX/TXT for mail.
3. Add destination address (personal Gmail) and confirm the verification email.
4. Create custom addresses: `hello@`, `support@` → that destination.
5. Enable **Catch-all** → same destination.

Expected MX targets (Cloudflare may show slight name variants; use whatever the dashboard adds):

- `route1.mx.cloudflare.net` / `route2.mx.cloudflare.net` / `route3.mx.cloudflare.net` (priorities as shown)

## Step 2 — Outbound: Gmail “Send mail as”

Cloudflare Routing does **not** send. In Gmail:

1. **Settings** → **Accounts** → **Send mail as** → Add `hello@kuchup.com` (and optionally `support@`).
2. Treat as alias; SMTP: `smtp.gmail.com`, port `587`, TLS, your Gmail username + [App Password](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords) (2FA required).
3. Complete the confirmation link Cloudflare forwards to Gmail.
4. Set default “From” to `hello@kuchup.com` if desired.

Expect occasional “via gmail.com” on some clients; fine for a solo product. Upgrade to Workspace / SMTP relay later only if deliverability becomes a problem.

## Step 3 — Auth records (critical SPF merge)

**One SPF TXT on the apex only.** Multiple SPF records break auth.

1. After Email Routing enable, open the apex SPF TXT Cloudflare created.
2. Merge Google for outbound into the **same** record, e.g.:

```text
v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net include:_spf.google.com ~all
```

(Keep whatever Cloudflare’s current `include:` is; only add `_spf.google.com` once — do not invent a second SPF TXT.)

3. Leave Cloudflare’s routing DKIM (`cf2024-1._domainkey` or dashboard equivalent) as-is.
4. Add DMARC (monitor first):

| Type | Name | Content |
|------|------|---------|
| TXT | `_dmarc` | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:hello@kuchup.com` |

Tighten to `p=quarantine` later after a week of clean tests.

## Step 4 — Verify

```bash
dig +short kuchup.com MX
dig +short kuchup.com TXT          # one SPF; GSC TXT still present
dig +short _dmarc.kuchup.com TXT
```

Manual checks:

1. From an external account → `hello@kuchup.com` → lands in Gmail (Routing).
2. Reply / compose From `hello@` → arrives; check headers or [mail-tester.com](https://www.mail-tester.com) for SPF pass.
3. Confirm Search Console still verified (GSC TXT unchanged).

## Step 5 — Document in repo

Add a short ops page (no secrets, no personal Gmail address):

- New: [`docs/operations/email.md`](docs/operations/email.md) — addresses, Routing + Gmail Send-as flow, SPF merge rule, DMARC, verify commands, “when to upgrade to Workspace”
- Link from [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) and a one-liner under Cloudflare DNS in [`docs/operations/ec2-panel.md`](docs/operations/ec2-panel.md)

Out of scope for this pass: homepage `mailto:`, transactional SES, Google Workspace.

## Who does what

| Work | Who |
|------|-----|
| Cloudflare dashboard + Gmail UI | You (credentials / inbox access) |
| Ops doc + README / ec2-panel links | Agent after you confirm this plan |

## Later (not now)

- Transactional mail from the app → AWS SES + separate `noreply@` / subdomain
- Real shared inbox / calendar → Google Workspace
- DMARC `p=quarantine` once monitoring is clean

# Domain email (kuchup.com)

Free inbound `@kuchup.com` via **Cloudflare Email Routing**, outbound via **Gmail Send mail as**. No mailbox product.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  sender[External sender] -->|to hello@kuchup.com| cfMX[Cloudflare MX]
  cfMX --> route[Email Routing]
  route --> gmail[Personal Gmail]
  gmail -->|Send as hello@ via smtp.gmail.com| world[Recipients]
```

## Addresses

| Address | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `hello@kuchup.com` | Public / product contact |
| `support@kuchup.com` | User help |
| Catch-all | Forward unknown `@kuchup.com` to the same destination |

Destination: one personal Gmail verified in Cloudflare. Do **not** put that personal address in this repo.

## Enable Cloudflare Email Routing

Cloudflare dashboard → **kuchup.com** → **Email** → **Email Routing**:

1. Enable / onboard the domain (Cloudflare adds MX + routing SPF/DKIM).
2. Confirm mail records are **DNS only** (grey cloud) — never orange-proxy MX or mail TXT.
3. Add a destination address (personal Gmail) and confirm the verification email.
4. Create custom addresses: `hello@`, `support@` → that destination.
5. Enable **Catch-all** → same destination.

Typical MX targets (use whatever the dashboard adds):

- `route1.mx.cloudflare.net`
- `route2.mx.cloudflare.net`
- `route3.mx.cloudflare.net`

Leave the existing Google Search Console verification TXT on the apex untouched.

## Outbound: Gmail Send mail as

Cloudflare Routing does **not** send mail.

1. Gmail → **Settings** → **See all settings** → **Accounts and Import** → **Send mail as** → **Add another email address**.
2. Name: e.g. `Kuchup`; address: `hello@kuchup.com` (repeat for `support@` if needed).
3. Treat as an alias. SMTP: `smtp.gmail.com`, port `587`, TLS.
4. Username: your Gmail address; password: a Google [App Password](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords) (2-Step Verification required).
5. Complete the confirmation link (Cloudflare forwards it to Gmail).
6. Optionally set default From to `hello@kuchup.com`.

Some clients may show “via gmail.com”. Acceptable for a solo product; move to Google Workspace or a dedicated SMTP relay only if deliverability becomes a problem.

## Auth records (SPF / DKIM / DMARC)

**One SPF TXT on the apex only.** Two SPF records break authentication.

After Email Routing is enabled, edit the apex SPF Cloudflare created and merge Google for outbound into the **same** record:

```text

```

Keep Cloudflare’s current `include:` if it differs; add `include:_spf.google.com` once. Do not add a second SPF TXT.

Leave Cloudflare’s routing DKIM (`cf2024-1._domainkey` or the selector shown in the dashboard) as-is.

Add DMARC (monitor first):

| Type | Name | Content |
|------|------|---------|
| TXT | `_dmarc` | `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:hello@kuchup.com` |

After a week of clean tests, consider tightening to `p=quarantine`.

## Verify

```bash
dig +short kuchup.com MX
dig +short kuchup.com TXT          # one SPF; GSC verification TXT still present
dig +short _dmarc.kuchup.com TXT
```

Manual checks:

1. From an external account → `hello@kuchup.com` → lands in the destination Gmail.
2. Compose From `hello@kuchup.com` → arrives; check headers or [mail-tester.com](https://www.mail-tester.com) for SPF pass.
3. Confirm Google Search Console still verified (GSC TXT unchanged).

## When to upgrade

| Need | Move to |
|------|---------|
| Shared inbox, Calendar, Drive as `@kuchup.com` | Google Workspace |
| App transactional mail (password reset, notifications) | AWS SES + `noreply@` or a mail subdomain |
| Stricter DMARC alignment / no “via gmail.com” | Workspace or SMTP relay with domain DKIM |

**Custom Token → Add permissions** like this:

| When you pick… | Permission | Level |
|----------------|------------|--------|

| **Zone** → Email Routing Rules | **Edit** | Zone |
| **Zone** → DNS | **Edit** | Zone |
| **Zone** → Zone | **Read** | Zone |

**Resources**

- **Account Resources:** Include → your account (the one that owns `kuchup.com`)
- **Zone Resources:** Include → Specific zone → `kuchup.com`

In the permission dropdown, type `Email Routing` — you should see **Email Routing Addresses** only after choosing **Account** as the first column (not Zone).

import json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error

TOKEN = os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN']
DEST = os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL_DESTINATION'].strip()
ZONE_NAME = os.environ.get('CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_NAME', 'kuchup.com')
BASE = 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4'

def api(method, path, body=None):
    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path,
        data=data,
        method=method,
        headers={
            'Authorization': f'Bearer {TOKEN}',
            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        },
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            payload = json.load(resp)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        err = e.read().decode()
        print(f'HTTP {e.code} {method} {path}\n{err}', file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)
    if not payload.get('success', True):
        print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)
    return payload

# 1) Zone
zones = api('GET', f'/zones?name={ZONE_NAME}')['result']
if not zones:
    raise SystemExit(f'zone not found: {ZONE_NAME}')
zone = zones[0]
zone_id = zone['id']
account_id = zone['account']['id']
print(f'zone_id={zone_id}')
print(f'account_id={account_id}')
print(f'status={zone["status"]}')

# 2) Current email routing settings
settings = api('GET', f'/zones/{zone_id}/email/routing')
print('routing_settings=', json.dumps(settings.get('result'), indent=2))

# 3) Enable DNS for email routing (creates MX/SPF/DKIM)
print('--- enabling email routing DNS ---')
try:
    enabled = api('POST', f'/zones/{zone_id}/email/routing/dns')
    print('dns_enable=', json.dumps(enabled.get('result'), indent=2))
except SystemExit:
    # maybe already enabled — try enable endpoint
    print('POST /dns failed or exited; trying /enable')
    pass

# re-check
settings = api('GET', f'/zones/{zone_id}/email/routing')
print('routing_after=', json.dumps(settings.get('result'), indent=2))
PY

import json, os, urllib.request, urllib.error, time

TOKEN = os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN']
DEST = os.environ['CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL_DESTINATION'].strip()
ZONE_ID = '93c36852d356be51548b4c0644df4c6c'
ACCOUNT_ID = 'f3e883f1a2290aac7b611f75cc8a7116'
ZONE = 'kuchup.com'
BASE = 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4'

def call(method, path, body=None):
    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        BASE + path, data=data, method=method,
        headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {TOKEN}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.load(resp)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode())

# 1) Create destination
code, payload = call('POST', f'/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/email/routing/addresses', {'email': DEST})
print('create_dest', code)
print(json.dumps({k: payload.get(k) for k in ('success','errors','messages')}, indent=2))
if payload.get('result'):
    r = payload['result']
    print('dest_id=', r.get('id'), 'verified=', r.get('verified'), 'email_domain=', DEST.split('@')[-1])

# List addresses again
code, addrs = call('GET', f'/accounts/{ACCOUNT_ID}/email/routing/addresses')
print('addr_count', len(addrs.get('result') or []))
for a in addrs.get('result') or []:
    print(' addr', a.get('email').split('@')[-1], 'verified=', a.get('verified'))

# 2) Create hello@ and support@ rules (may fail until dest verified)
for local in ('hello', 'support'):
    body = {
        'name': f'{local} forward',
        'enabled': True,
        'matchers': [{'type': 'literal', 'field': 'to', 'value': f'{local}@{ZONE}'}],
        'actions': [{'type': 'forward', 'value': [DEST]}],
    }
    code, payload = call('POST', f'/zones/{ZONE_ID}/email/routing/rules', body)
    print(f'rule_{local}', code, 'success=', payload.get('success'), 'err=', (payload.get('errors') or [{}])[0].get('message'))

# 3) Update catch-all to forward
body = {
    'matchers': [{'type': 'all'}],
    'actions': [{'type': 'forward', 'value': [DEST]}],
    'enabled': True,
    'name': 'catch all',
}
code, payload = call('PUT', f'/zones/{ZONE_ID}/email/routing/rules/catch_all', body)
print('catch_all', code, 'success=', payload.get('success'), 'err=', (payload.get('errors') or [{}])[0].get('message'))

# 4) Manually ensure MX records
desired_mx = [
    (92, 'route1.mx.cloudflare.net'),
    (27, 'route2.mx.cloudflare.net'),
    (56, 'route3.mx.cloudflare.net'),
]
# Check existing MX
code, existing = call('GET', f'/zones/{ZONE_ID}/dns_records?type=MX&per_page=100')
print('existing_mx', [(r.get('priority'), r.get('content')) for r in existing.get('result') or []])

for prio, host in desired_mx:
    already = any(
        r.get('content', '').rstrip('.').lower() == host and r.get('name') in (ZONE, f'{ZONE}.')
        for r in (existing.get('result') or [])
    )
    if already:
        print('mx exists', prio, host)
        continue
    code, payload = call('POST', f'/zones/{ZONE_ID}/dns_records', {
        'type': 'MX',
        'name': ZONE,
        'content': host,
        'priority': prio,
        'ttl': 1,
        'proxied': False,
    })
    print('create_mx', host, code, 'success=', payload.get('success'), 'err=', (payload.get('errors') or [{}])[0].get('message'))
